facts.claim: Redwire reported Q2 2026 revenue of $117.074 million and first-half 2026 revenue of $214.046 million in its filed Form 10-Q.

The filed Q2 2026 segment data show first-half Space revenue of $107.859 million and Defense Tech revenue of $106.187 million; management attributes $85.6 million of the year-over-year revenue increase to the Edge Autonomy acquisition, limiting clean organic comparability.
First-half 2026 net loss was $117.473 million, while equity-based compensation expense was $50.635 million, preserving a material gap between revenue growth and self-funding economics.

Redwire's revenue mix in the filed 10-Q included $99.099 million of first-half 2026 national-security revenue, $38.197 million civil-space revenue and $76.750 million commercial/other revenue, evidencing diversified end-market exposure but meaningful government-program dependence.

risks.risk: Acquisition-driven growth materially affects year-over-year comparability; the filed 10-Q attributes $85.6 million of first-half revenue growth to Edge Autonomy.
Large first-half net loss and equity compensation remain material despite stronger revenue and gross-profit trends.

contradictions.contradiction: Rapid reported revenue expansion coexists with a $117.473 million first-half net loss, and much of the year-over-year revenue increase is acquisition-related rather than clean organic growth.
contradictions.disposition: Source-addressed primary filing evidence sharpens rather than resolves the existing growth-versus-cash-economics tension; Alpha should incorporate it into underwriting and confidence.

unknowns.unknown: A complete Alpha score still requires source-addressed market valuation and any remaining factor/risk/confidence inputs; Scout does not construct the numeric score.
